anomalies.observed: The MCU clock pin PB13 (U2 pin 34) does not connect directly to DISP_SCL. It goes to U5 pin 2 on net Net-(U5-Pad2). U5 (74LVC1G34 buffer) drives U5 pin 4 onto DISP_SCL, which also carries R6 pin 1 and U4 pin 18 (D0). The buffer sits in the I2C clock path to the OLED.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes DISP_SCL as U2 pin 34 (PB13) through R6 (10 kOhm pull-up) to U4 pin 18 (D0), a direct connection. It does not list U5 or any buffer, and states that the MCU and display are connected directly.

evidence.quote: `DISP_SCL`: U2 pin 34 (`PB13`) — R6 (10 kΩ) to VCC — U4 pin 18 (`D0`)
No MCU other than U2 appears.

anomalies.impact: The display clock is routed through an unlisted logic buffer. The buffer adds propagation delay and alters the I2C clock drive. It also adds a part whose power, grounding and function are undocumented. This could break or destabilise OLED communication compared with the intended direct connection.

anomalies.observed: The STM32 VBAT pin (U2 pin 1) sits alone on its own net with no connection to VDD or to a battery.
anomalies.expected: On the STM32L4, VBAT must be tied to a supply (commonly VDD) when no battery is used. Leaving it floating can cause RTC and backup-domain problems.
anomalies.impact: The backup domain and RTC may be unpowered or unreliable. The main run-time firmware behaviour is likely unaffected, so confidence is lower.
